rows.question: I was wondering - how many adults in Canada lack a regular primary care provider?
rows.answer: The 2025 OurCare survey (16,299 respondents, April to July 2025) estimated that about 5.9 million adults in Canada lack a regular family doctor, nurse practitioner or primary care team [1]. In 2022, about 35% of adults aged 18 to 29 reported having no primary care provider [1]. People without a regular provider commonly use walk-in clinics, virtual walk-in clinics or emergency departments for non-urgent problems [1].
